text: A uniformly charged disc of radius R having surface charge density $σ$ is placed in the xy plane with its center at the origin. Find the electric field intensity along the z-axis at a distance Z from origin :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Consider a small ring of radius r and thickness dr on disc.


[IMG]

area of elemental ring on disc

dA = 2$π$rdr

$dEz=\frac{kdqz}{(z^{2}+r^{2})^{3/2}}$

$E=\int\limits _{0}^{R}dE_{z}=\frac{σ}{2\in _{0}}\left [1-\frac{z}{\sqrt{R^{2}+z^{2}}}\right ]$

text: A balloon carries a total load of 185 kg at normal pressure and temperature of 27${}^{\circ }$C. What load will the balloon carry on rising to a height at which the barometric pressure is 45 cm of Hg and the temperature is $-$7${}^{\circ }$C. Assuming the volume constant?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
PM = $ρ$RT

$\therefore$ $\frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\frac{ρ_{1}T_{1}}{ρ_{2}T_{2}}$

$\frac{ρ_{1}}{ρ_{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{P_{1}T_{2}}{P_{2}T_{1}}=\left (\frac{76}{45}\right )\times \frac{266}{300}$

$\frac{ρ_{1}}{ρ_{2}}\Rightarrow \frac{M_{1}}{M_{2}}=\frac{76\times 266}{45\times 300}$

$\therefore$ $M_{2}\Rightarrow \frac{45\times 300\times 185}{76\times 266}=123.54$ kg
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: An object is placed beyond the centre of curvature C of the given concave mirror. If the distance of the object is $d_{1}$ from C and the distance of the image formed is $d_{2}$ from C, the radius of curvature of this mirror is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Distances are measured from the pole, negative in front of the mirror. The object lies a distance $d_{1}$ beyond C, so $u=-(R+d_{1})$. An object beyond C forms a real image between F and C, a distance $d_{2}$ from C towards the mirror, so $v=-(R-d_{2})$. For a concave mirror $f=-\dfrac{R}{2}$.

Mirror formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{f}\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{R-d_{2}}+\dfrac{1}{R+d_{1}}=\dfrac{2}{R}$

$R(2R+d_{1}-d_{2})=2(R+d_{1})(R-d_{2})=2R^{2}+2Rd_{1}-2Rd_{2}-2d_{1}d_{2}$

$R(d_{1}-d_{2})=2d_{1}d_{2}\Rightarrow R=\dfrac{2d_{1}d_{2}}{d_{1}-d_{2}}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text:
A huge circular arc of length 4.4 ly subtends an angle of 4″ (4 seconds of arc) at the centre of the circle. How long it would take for a body to complete 4 revolutions if its speed is 8 AU per second?

Given : 1 ly = 9.46 $\times$ $10^{15} m$

1 AU = 1.5 $\times$ $10^{11} m$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$R=\frac{l}{θ}$

Time $=\frac{4\times 2πR}{v}=\frac{4\times 2π}{v}\left (\frac{l}{θ}\right )$

put l = 4.4 $\times$ 9.46 $\times$ $10^{15}$

v = 8 $\times$ 1.5 $\times$ $10^{11}$

$θ=\frac{4}{3600}\times \frac{π}{180}$ rad.

we get time = 4.5 $\times$ $10^{10} \sec $.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: An ideal gas is expanding such that $PT^{3} =$ constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$PT^{3} =$ constant

$\left (\frac{nRT}{v}\right )T^{3} =$ constant

$T^{4} V^{-1} =$ constant

$T^{4} = kV$

$\Rightarrow 4\frac{\Delta T}{T}=\frac{\Delta V}{V}$ ....... (1)

$\Delta$V = V$γ\Delta$T ........ (2)

comparing (1) and (2), we get

$γ=\frac{4}{T}$

text: A uniform conducting wire of length 24a and resistance R is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of an equilateral triangle of side 'a' and then in the form of a square of side 'a'. The coil is connected to a voltage source $V_{0}$. The ratio of magnetic moment of the coils in case of equilateral triangle to that for square is 1 : $\sqrt{y}$ where y is ................. .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In triangle shape $N_{t}=\frac{24a}{3a}=8$

In square $N_{s}=\frac{24a}{4a}=6$

$\frac{M_{t}}{M_{s}}=\frac{N_{t}IA_{t}}{N_{s}IA_{s}}$ [I will be same in both]

$=\frac{8\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times a^{2}}{6\times a^{2}}$

$\frac{M_{t}}{M_{s}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

y = 3

text: First, a set of n equal resistors of 10 $\Omega$ each are connected in series to a battery of emf 20V and internal resistance 10$\Omega$. A current I is observed to flow. Then, the n resistors are connected in parallel to the same battery. It is observed that the current is increased 20 times, then the value of n is ............... .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In series

$R_{eq}=nR=10n$

$i_{s}=\frac{20}{10+10n}=\frac{2}{1+n}$

In parallel

$R_{eq}=\frac{10}{n}$

$i_{p}=\frac{20}{\frac{10}{n}+10}=\frac{2n}{1+n}$

$\frac{i_{p}}{i_{s}}=20$

$\frac{\left (\frac{2n}{1+n}\right )}{\left (\frac{2}{1+n}\right )}=20$

$n=20$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text:
A rod CD of thermal resistance $10.0 KW^{-1}$ is joined at the middle of an identical rod AB as shown in figure. The end A, B and D are maintained at 200${}^{\circ }$C, 100${}^{\circ }$C and 125${}^{\circ }$C respectively. The heat current in CD is P watt. The value of P is ................. .


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The rods are identical, so $R_{AB}=R_{CD}=10\text{K W}^{-1}$ (kelvin per watt). C is the mid-point of AB, so $R_{AC}=R_{CB}=5\text{K W}^{-1}$.

Let the junction C be at temperature $T$. The heat current from A into C equals the heat currents leaving C through CB and CD:

$\dfrac{200-T}{5}=\dfrac{T-100}{5}+\dfrac{T-125}{10}$

$400-2T=2T-200+T-125\Rightarrow 5T=725\Rightarrow T=145{}^{\circ }\text{C}$

Heat current in CD: $P=\dfrac{145-125}{10}=2\text{W}$.

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift

text: Two persons A and B perform same amount of work in moving a body through a certain distance d with application of forces acting at angle 45${}^{\circ }$ and 60${}^{\circ }$ with the direction of displacement respectively. The ratio of force applied by person A to the force applied by person B is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$. The value of x is .................... .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $W_{A} = W_{B}$

$F_{A}d \cos 45{}^{\circ }$ $= F_{B}d \cos 60{}^{\circ }$

$F_{A}\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=F_{B}\times \frac{1}{2}$

$\frac{F_{A}}{F_{B}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

x = 2
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 27th August Morning Shift
